utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, do you intend to ask the witness about any of the specific allegations of deportation in paragraph 63?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the questions I'm going to ask him now have to do with the overall conduct vis-a-vis the movement and displacement of civilians and the attitude they took. When I say "they," I mean those who represented the authorities in Kosovo and Metohija during that period of time and their treatment of civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For example, paragraph 63(k)(ii) alleges that forces of the FRY on 27th and 28th of March 1999 attacked the town of Kacanik and they harassed, detained, beat and shot many Kosovo Albanian residents of Kacanik. "Thousands of persons fled to nearby forests and eventually walked across the border into Macedonia." Do you have any specific information about that, that incident, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not, Your Honour Mr. President. All I can say is that the formulation according to which the forces Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. attacked the town really doesn't correspond to the truth. And I've explained this on several occasions, what the goals of police intervention were when the police intervened. We never ever had the object of attacking any town, and that formulation, that phrase means -- would mean that we wanted to destroy something, and that really didn't correspond to the efforts made by the police and army and their goals and objectives in their anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So what you can say in relation to that allegation is that it is inconsistent with your understanding of how the police behaved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting, perhaps I could tell you my personal experience with respect to certain groups of refugees that were moving towards Albanian, for instance. So I personally took care of this large movement of civilians. One day towards the end of March or around about that date I went to Malisevo, for example. Malisevo is a well-known place as being a stronghold of the KLA. That's what it's known for. And when I got there, I came across about 30.000, maybe more, people who were on tractors, who were in different vehicles, expecting somebody to send them buses and trucks to transport them further on to Albanian. I spent, with a group of my associates and people from Prizren, at least two hours, maybe three hours, talking to the people, talking to these people and trying to convince them to go back home, to go back to their villages and homes, and I guaranteed that the police would not do anything but protect them. And in Malisevo, together with the civilians, there were a large number of policemen who communicated with the people, and they were very tolerant, highly tolerant, and did their best to convince them that we're not there to persecute them in any way but to help them and to protect them from persecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And did you ascertain from any of them why they had left their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they were very reticent in talking to us at all. Their position was that they were mistrustful, distrustful. But usually the answer given was NATO. Whether that was indeed what they thought, I believe it was. I can't, of course, claim that it was, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me about the state policy with respect to this displacement of civilians and what you yourself as the leadership of the police force conducted and what you saw was implemented by the staff in Pristina, for example.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that I saw myself clearly indicated the concern that existed with regard to the situation and that everything was done to prevent this exodus. The only thing was that we didn't wish to exert pressure and prevent them from leaving forcibly. We considered that that wouldn't be conducive to the rights of citizens to leave territory of their own free will if it came into the war zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at tabs 82 onwards, General, please. They are documents which are linked to the conduct and behaviour of the police. For example, tab 82. Take a look at tab 82 now, please, and tell us what it contains. It is a dispatch, I believe, a telegram. Have you found that tab, General?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- we have a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Since there is a translation, then it's easier for us to go through this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Whose dispatch is this?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the dispatch from the MUP staff in Pristina. It is dated the 15th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Is it addressed to all the organs of the MUP in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that, that it is sent to the units stipulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Despite the fact that on the 5th of April, 1999, an order was issued to prevent civilians from leaving their place of residence and to guarantee their safety (and take security measures to protect this population), it was observed that some commanding officers addressed here are not obeying the order and tolerate departure of civilian population on a massive scale." Paragraph two reads as follows: "Therefore --" it's not a very legible copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "All the measures..."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "All the measures ordered regarding the police members' treatment of the civilian population must be implemented consistently and any deviation from the order issued brings with it accountability. Inform the staff in writing of any problems." Those are the contents of the dispatch that the MUP sent out to all units in the field. And from this dispatch we can see what I explained a moment ago in answering the previous questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, what do we have in tab 183? Let's skip the first part. Once again it has been sent by the staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tab 83, do you mean, not 183?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 83. 83. The next tab. We were dealing with tab 82. The next tab is 83.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As we were saying, this was addressed to all the police organs in Kosovo and Metohija, as we can see; is that right? Is there anybody who was left out?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that all the organisational units in Kosovo and Metohija received this, and the dispatch is dated the 20th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Now, what does it say as the subject?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the subjects are the displaced population or refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then we find, "Please find attached an order of the 3rd Army commander, Colonel General Nebojsa Pavkovic, regarding treatment of refugees."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And then we have the order from the commander of the 3rd Army as an attachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say at the top? It says that the subject is care of refugees, and then Order.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the order by the commander of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does it say exactly?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it all? It says: "As a result of the unending air raids of the NATO forces on the units of the army of Yugoslavia and the expected aggression by the ground forces, the number of movements of the civilian population in the unit's areas of responsibility has increased thus significantly complicating the overall security situation. With a view to protecting the civilian population and directing them to safer areas, I hereby order," et cetera. And then the order contains a total of nine points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, now, what is being ordered? We see that this is an order issued to protect the population and to direct them to safer areas. What does point 1 stipulate? What?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The corps commands and MUP organs shall establish the exact distribution and number of refugees in their areas of responsibility and extend to them through the competent organs the necessary help in food and other necessities," and they're referring to the refugee population, displaced population. Point 2 says: "They shall identify villages outside the areas of unit deployment in the areas of responsibility where the refugees can be accommodated." Point 3 reads as follows: "They shall monitor each day movements of the civilian population in their areas of responsibility and ensure for them the necessary protection and return to their homes or areas outside the areas of combat operations." Do you want me to read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that we would need to do so because point 4 reads: "They shall protect the refugees and their property in the villages --"

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "... in the villages and specified areas from the operations of the STS --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does that mean; Siptar terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Siptar terrorist forces "and attacks by other persons in the territory." "5: They shall take vigorous measures to prevent the appropriation of personal effects and private property of the refugees. Criminal charges shall be brought against the perpetrators. "6: They shall prevent the arson of houses and other structures owned by the Siptars in their areas of responsibility. "7: They shall take measures through the authorities to extend to the refugees help in food and required medical assistance. "8: They shall take all security measure in the areas of refugee reception and protection to shield them from the STS operations - Siptar operations - from the territory among the refugees."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then, finally, it says that areas should be pinpointed where they can be sent to for safety.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in keeping with an order of this kind, did everybody behave along those lines lower down the chain?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an order which was binding. It had to be applied at all levels down the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now tab 84 is one that we have already looked at when we discussed another topic during your testimony, so I don't want to dwell on it now. You've already quoted portions of that tab and we discussed it during your testimony, but tell us, please, what the other tabs contain, tabs 85 to 87 inclusive.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite obviously correspondence between one police unit and the staff in Pristina, the headquarters in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it recommends certain points and accommodation, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the first note, tab 85, where the command of the 122nd Intervention Brigade informs the staff of the lines reached. Of course, codes are used to denote those lines, so we have figures here denoting the lines reached. And they say that positions are 78 to 90 and 111 to 90 and 92. And I'm -- I propose points 138 and 139, and is asking that these persons be accommodated in these two recommended points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: To move them geographically to areas of safety?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And he expects the staff to answer along those lines, and the army is asked to tell them whether those are points of safety and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just briefly, this dispatch that was sent to the Pec SUP, for instance, what is this Djurdjevdan operation, that civilians should be returned to their place of residence and all security measures taken?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a dispatch by the MUP staff dated the 8th of May, sent to the SUP of Djakovica with respect to the return of civilians to their original place of residence after an anti-terrorist activity, which is coded once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do we also find an answer to the previous dispatch that was sent where accommodation was asked for? That's tab 86, the last document there, where it says, "Civilians should be returned to their villages, and if that is not possible, then we agree to them being accommodated in the areas you have designated."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is an answer to the dispatch from the 122nd Brigade where they suggested the areas they should be accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In tab 87, there is a document entitled "Accommodation situation for refugees in the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija on the 19th of April, 1999."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Not to go through all of this now in great detail, Pec, Gnjilane, Djakovica, Urosevac, these are actually all the secretariats of the interior?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the secretariats. In the first paragraph you can see that on that day the total number registered was 2.300 -- 231.780 refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Some were staying in homes and others in the open?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just leave -- look at the first sentence. "According to reports from SUP concluding on the 19th of April, about 231.780 refugees have been registered, mostly accommodated in family and friends' houses, in large-scale accommodation facilities, and in the open."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then information is provided, for example, for Djakovica. What does it say about Djakovica, the SUP of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't have to read all of it.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... assistance was offered to 6.700 refugees, members of the Albanian ethnic community, for them to return to the area where they're resident in Kosovska Mitrovica and Vucitrn municipalities."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that is the 18th of April, 1999 when, according to what Mr. Nice claims, the police was evicting Albanians.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "They were offered assistance in the form of transport and foodstuffs. At about 1300 hours on the 19th of April, 1999 assistance was given to the final group of about 4.500 refugees to return to Kosovska Mitrovica, Vucitrn, and Srbica municipalities..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "... to their places of residence"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... to their places of residence."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let me just have a look. I have another tab noted here that we should look at with regard to these questions. Let me just have a look. I think we already looked at this. All right. General, we've seen a few of these examples. What was the attitude of international organisations towards refugees?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during the war itself I at least was not in a position to see the activity of any international organisation there. Possibly they were there, but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Before the war operations started, that is to say before the 24th of March, there were different international organisations there.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. During 1998 and all the way up to the war there were different international organisations there. I do not have a great deal of knowledge about their attitude towards civilians, but I do know of a case that I witnessed myself and that I have already referred to. Istinic, the end of the summer of 1998, when I was directly involved in returning tens of thousands of Albanians to their places of residence, to their homes after a terrorist campaign. I had a serious problem with a team of the International Red Cross, I think it was the International Red Cross. There is a telegram about that. And practically behind our backs they were trying to persuade more influential Albanians not to act in accordance with what we were saying at all because that would be a bad choice for them. In spite of these problems, during three or four days we managed to return all the internally displaced persons from Istinic to their places of residence. And I wish to note that in that group of civilians there were several terrorists and a large quantity of weapons that were handed over. I explained that in greater detail a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In relation to what you're saying, in tab 81 there is a letter of General Lukic to the minister of the interior, to his office. It says: "Our information number 13/98 of the 13th of September, 1998." That is a document that has to do with what you were talking about just now, the village of Istinic where you were personally?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is quite certainly the incident concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And now the name of this representative of the international organisation is mentioned. This is the third paragraph: "When the policemen called on the representatives of the Siptar ethnic minority from Istinic and other villages to return to their homes, this person warned them on several occasions and asked the people present to return to their homes because it was not safe, thus causing panic, insecurity, and uncertainty among the residents on whether to return or not."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an absolutely accurate description. I do not know which organisation she belongs here -- ah, yes, I see here: Representative of the International Red Cross from the Belgrade mission. That's what it says in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in relation to this treatment of persons who had left their homes, what can you say about the campaign regarding the reporting of residence of displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the tab that we skipped a few minutes ago. That is tab 84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I believe there is a specific reference to this village -- municipality, rather, in tab 8 -- tab 81, in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. 63, 63(l). This is September --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll have to have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: September 1998. The allegation in 63(l) relates Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to the 29th of March, 1999, and it speaks of an attack by forces of the FRY and Serbia, men and women ordered to undress. You see, I'm trying to relate the evidence to specific incidents in the indictment, if it is possible, but this document in tab 81 does relate to the charge but to September 1998. How is that assisting your case, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Robinson, I'm trying to establish how the police behaved in respect of the movement of the population, what the police did by way of assistance. We went through a few documents where orders are given to take care of the civilian population. All these measures and orders are totally incompatible with what is stated in the indictment. If what the indictment says were true, then it would be quite impossible to have such orders and such positions taken by the police. It is impossible to have orders like this that we've been quoting here, and these orders say how to help the population, how to give them food, shelter, how to put them into safe areas, and that is quite incompatible with what the indictment says. It is in total contradiction. Documents from the area concerned are in total contradiction to the -- to the indictment. That simply cannot be the case. The police and the military cannot behave in contravention of the orders they receive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A wide gap between what is in an order and the actual enforcement of it. I am reminded of the time I spent on the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights. We visited many countries, on-site visits, and some of the worst offenders had the best written laws to protect human rights. But carry on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, this doesn't have to do with laws and regulations. Only they have -- this has to do with orders as well. As far as the police is concerned, before General Stevanovic, I had Colonel Paponjak here, who was speaking from a local level about conduct in terms of the implementation of orders that he received. Now we have General Stevanovic who is talking about the conduct throughout the province, and we're going to see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Carry on with the questioning. We must conclude this witness's examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 63 that you mentioned a few moments ago, that the assertions regarding Kotlina are contained there too. That is in (k)(i). We presented very clear documents about that yesterday which are -- which totally contradict what it says here. Kotlina, speaking of murders and also persecutions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue with the -- continue with your questions. Continue with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, just give us the briefest possible answers. You said that there was this campaign about registering places of residence. That is generally known, but what can you say about that, for temporarily displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The objective was to deal with that number of internally displaced persons - we saw the figure in a document that we looked at recently - to deal with it statistically according to the places where they were staying, to have documents in this respect in addition to all the measures that are ordered in the tab that we skipped, including local security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. You've been repeating this, that we've skipped that. So in tab 84, that is the document signed by General Lukic of the ministry staff. I'm going to ask you about number 1. "Organise a residence registration service in all places accommodating refugees who had left their domicile --"

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "-- due to bombing by NATO forces. In the registration of domicile include persons who have not registered their place of domicile but were found at their address where they are living."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Make it possible for all persons to register their residence on the established form number, and issue certificates of residence registration."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We've been through this. Move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was the aim of this campaign?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aim was to regulate the affairs of the displaced persons in the places where they were staying temporarily. That was used for two purposes; security and taking care -- security of the persons concerned and their general safety. There were statistics at border crossings. That's where statistics were kept, when the persons crossed international borders, but not persons crossing to Montenegro or Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was only at the state border.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 63, with regard to all the allegations, it is stated that the personal documents were taken from Albanians who were going to Albania and Macedonia, that the police were taking their documents. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that from the indictment, or the presentation of the indictment, but this wording is really a generalisation of perhaps a particular incident at a particular border crossing. Perhaps I even saw a film about this. But I claim that, as I have said several times, that this is not part of any policy pursued or orders issued. This was excessive behaviour on the part of a particular shift at a particular point in time at a particular border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, now I'm asking you about a person who professionally dealt with police matters for many years. If a person's documents had been taken away, would that deprive him or her of the possibility of ascertaining his or her identity or jeopardising his or her status or whatever?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You dealt with that already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, yesterday we showed the electronic system of registering citizens. Would anybody who was familiar with this system get the idea that he should prevent the return of citizens to the country by taking away their personal documents?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... mere speculation about what other people in general might do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Move on to another area. You've dealt with this already. I said so. Move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honour. May I just make a comment about this qualification speculation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. Move on to another question, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I'm going to ask you about a concept which is often mentioned here; shelling and devastation of buildings. In many paragraphs, reference is made to a particular wording or, rather, a pattern. Forces of Serbia and FRY go into a particular place, separate men from women following shelling, et cetera, et cetera. That is the wording frequently used. I'm going to ask you, during clashes with terrorists, did the police and the military destroy civilian buildings?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Destruction of civilian facilities was never the purpose of any operation carried out in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did devastation of facilities in Kosovo and Metohija occur?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the term "devastation" could encompass. If we take it to mean deliberate destruction of buildings, that certainly didn't happen in Kosovo and Metohija. That was not our practice and would have served no purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to your understanding and the understanding of the Ministry of the Interior, would buildings whose purpose was normally civilian but which are used as a place from which to shoot at the police and the military continue to be regarded as civilian facilities?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They are no longer regarded as civilian facilities. But even then, the purpose of the police and the army is not to destroy such facilities. They only seek to suppress the armed resistance coming from such facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any considerable discrepancies in the degree of destruction of buildings from one place to another since you travelled a lot across Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed large differences in terms of the degree of destruction between various places in Kosovo. I can cite an example. The greatest number of destroyed buildings could be seen in the area of Suva Reka, in the area of Pec, whereas many, many villages I passed were absolutely intact. As an example of that, I can cite Rogovo between Djakovica and Prizren, the town of Prizren, the town of Urosevac, Gnjilane, Pristina. For instance, the villages around Gnjilane were almost intact. The villages, rather, around Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you don't mean to include destruction by NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And were there any cases of damage or destruction to public utilities, infrastructure?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I know of, or very rarely. If such facilities, infrastructure were damaged, that was always by terrorists, so that all the public utilities, electricity, water supply and such things functioned quite well under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were there on the spot. You travelled a lot. Tell me, could you distinguish clearly between destruction caused by NATO airstrikes and destruction or damage resulting from clashes between our forces and the KLA?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Maybe not in a few specific cases, but it was normally very clear what was caused by NATO bombing and what was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it still possible that certain civilian facilities were destroyed by our forces beyond what was necessary in terms of anti-terrorist combat?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could only have been part of incidents and excessive behaviour, but I don't know of any such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you about paramilitary groups and volunteers. According to your information, were paramilitary formations active in Kosovo and Metohija? Do you know of any paramilitary formation that was under any sort of control by any body or state authority?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paramilitary units under the control of the state authorities in any form did not exist that I know of. There could have been uniformed or un-uniformed armed groups that could have committed occasionally criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But in view of the disposition of police forces and military forces, could there have been an important paramilitary unit that they failed to notice?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paramilitary units could have been active and present as something beyond and contrary to the law but not under the control of the police or the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information of the activity of such groups from other wars in other areas of ex-Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with some paramilitary groups that were active in the territory of ex-Yugoslavia from 1991 onwards, and I know that members of some such groups had residence on the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they ever active on the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Moreover, all members of such groups identified in Serbia were arrested, their weapons, if found, were seized, and they were instructed that if they wished to join the army they had to follow the regular procedure, and whether they were eventually accepted into the army depended on the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now we are talking about the beginning of the 1990s. Did the police take any action, conduct any operation on the territory of ex-Yugoslavia together with such a paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And during the 1990s, what was the attitude of the authorities of Serbia toward such paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was extremely negative, and I've already stated what measures were taken against members of such groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us return to Kosovo and Metohija again, General. Have you ever heard of any paramilitary unit in Kosovo and Metohija? Did you have any information about the presence of such a group in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia participate or assist in the arming of any group outside their own personnel?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police of Serbia armed only its own reservists, but the reserve force of the police are an integral part of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you've mentioned 1990s, what particular paramilitary units and groups did you hear about in those years?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of various units in the Republic of Serbian Krajina, in Republika Srpska, such as the Serbian Volunteers Guard, Green Berets, Red Berets, the National Guard Corps, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You are talking about paramilitary units on various sites?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on various sites. Some of them belonged to various state bodies or party organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the Red Berets. What units were known under that name?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name Red Berets was extremely -- extremely popular. Every unit wanted to be called the Red Berets, and any unit that included in its uniform a red beret often assumed that name, so that there was a multitude of units that were mistakenly known as Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does that mean? In which area?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbian Krajina, in the Republic of Serbia itself, but also the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the Republic of Serbia, who wore red berets?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of a special anti-terrorist unit that wore red berets, and the citizens called them Red Berets. There was another unit in the special forces of the VJ also wore red berets, and the citizens called them Red Berets. Arkan's Guard also wore red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A question was raised here about the date of establishment of this unit for special operations of the Serbian police, the JSO.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They, too, wore red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When was it established?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the spring of 1996, according to my information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what information do you have?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was invited to attend the ceremony that was organised on the occasion of their establishment. I believe it was in the spring of 1996. I can't be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you personally attended the ceremony of establishment of that unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it was in the spring of 1996?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it was raining.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We will now move on to some issues, and we will refer to the documents we have here related to various meetings which discussed these problems. So we're talking about meetings, not regulations, not orders, but specific meetings. Let me ask you first: Did you attend various meetings that discussed state policy regarding the situation in Kosovo and Metohija, combat against terrorism, and what was the official state policy at the time, anyway?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended several such meetings, and I've already explained what the policy of state authorities was regarding the need to combat terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend the meeting that was held at the staff of the Ministry of the Interior in Pristina on the 21st of December, 1998?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check, because I attended most such meetings, but I don't remember them by dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I expect from you anyway, because we have precise records of all these meetings, tab by tab. Look, for instance, at tab 68.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Good. Is this the record of the meeting of the ministry staff that included the minister of the interior and chiefs of secretariats held in Pristina? We can see that you were present too.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see that in the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in the -- and in the third paragraph, the minister says: "The conditions of work are complex. Although we defeated terrorists and seized their weapons." Does it follow from this that it was not their objective to kill the terrorists, just to disarm them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The objective was to neutralise, to liquidate the terrorist organisation, not to kill the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On page --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where is that paragraph, Mr. Milosevic? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He said it's paragraph 3 but I can't find it on the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 would be on page 2?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 2, the end of Minister Stojiljkovic's comment: "... even though we defeated the terrorists and took away their weapons."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 in the original Serbian version, in the second sentence of this paragraph it says literally: "The main task of the police is to protect and defend the country from such terrorist actions and criminals."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's the second paragraph on the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note it's page 3, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The most important item was for the police to maintain control of the area and secure free passage and -- We are going to go through this rather quickly. The sub-heading seems to say "Assessments, conclusions." It says: "Every campaign and operation of the police has to have an objective and has to be reported to the OSCE mission." Have you found this?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Read this line.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Every activity of the police has to have a specific reason and must be notified to the OSCE mission. Every action must be taken in keeping with the regulations and the law, not in a soldierly way. There must not be any looting or pillage during police activities. The police should act professionally and lawfully as it did in Kapasnica [phoen], Pec and Glodjane."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Reference is made to the OSCE mission although it seems to be inclined or to sympathise with the terrorists. "They must be allowed to stay."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, the conclusion says that the following actions need to be taken. What is written in this section? I would like to mention just a few things.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fourth line from the bottom says: "Weapons should be used only in self-defence and only proportionately to the force of attack."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's in the document, but before that, it says: "In order to use heavy weapons and large calibre weapons, we must be provoked (attacked) by heavy weapons. We cannot take heavy weapons and equipment in our vehicles."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes that's in keeping with our rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "The police should act as if we were working in Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I do wish the accused would recognise that not only I but, more important, the Court has to be able to follow documents. There's very little point in just racing through them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I've mentioned this to you before that leading evidence is not a private dialogue between yourself and the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I understood it that you do have a translation of this document, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have it, but proper protocol requires that you identify the passage and you must not proceed until the Chamber has found it so that we can follow it. That's not only a matter of courtesy, it also goes to the efficiency of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the impression that you were able to follow because I identified the subtitle on the basis of -- based on that which was presented, it was concluded that "The following should be undertaken," and then that's the passage after that. Now, under that heading we also find the bullet points and the various positions. I could read them all, but to avoid reading them all I quoted just some of them. At the end of the seventh bullet point, it says: "In order to use heavy weapons and large calibre weapons we must be provoked, that is to say attacked also by heavy weapons. We cannot take heavy weapons and equipment in our vehicles." Have you found that passage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And underneath, the next bullet point that I quoted is the following: "The police should act as if we are working in Belgrade." And then five lower down, just one line, it says: "Use weapons only in self-defence and in proportion to the strength of the attack." So that's what I wanted to quote. I hope you found those passages now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did the police behave in keeping with these instructions?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This had the aim of having the police act in conformity with this, and all the leaders had orders to implement all conclusions from this type of meeting. Therefore, the police did act accordingly, according to these instructions and guidelines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 69, General, we have the minutes of a meeting that took place on the 17th of February in Pristina, 1999. Did you attend that meeting in the MUP headquarters?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And you can see that from what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who else attended and what did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has a list of members attending, or persons attending the meeting. And the question discussed was the security situation and the tasks stipulated, and we can see that from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let's just go briefly through this document. On page 2, the last paragraph, which begins with the following words: "Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic," it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope, Mr. Robinson, that will be readily identified by you, the passage. It begins on page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note page 3, "Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to skip over that first portion and then I shall go on to quote from the middle of the paragraph. He assessed that the basic problem in Kosovo was terrorism and separatism by certain members of the Siptar ethnic minority. Is the minister making a clear distinction between Albanians and separatists and terrorists there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that. Insistence was always made on a clear distinction between terrorists and the other citizens of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, it says: "He assessed that since the arrival of the OSCE mission the number of terrorist attacks and provocations had increased but without any significant consequences." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then he goes on to say, because he is a government member and minister of the interior: "The state of Serbia will do everything in its power to resolve the problems in Kosovo by peaceful and political means. Kosovo will be multi-ethnic and a part of the existing constitutional and legal system of Serbia and the FRY."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then on the next page, since the date is as it stands, the 17th of February, that is to say just prior to the aggression, very close to the aggression, we have direct reference to the tasks, the forthcoming tasks of the police force to mop up the territory of terrorists. So once again reference is made to terrorists. And then the next bullet point, gathering intelligence and information about the movements to eliminate misinformation and propaganda, then to maintain law and order, ensure personal and property safety in the fight against terrorism and crime. Can you find that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those are conclusions as to forthcoming tasks, because the aim of the meeting was to analyse the security situation and to determine tasks for the forthcoming period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Fine. RPO. Could you remind me of what that abbreviation is?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reserve police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it says: "Tell the PRO -- RPO and the people that civil war must be avoided at all cost but that in case of conflict the aggressor should be killed, not women and children."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a message to reserve police units whose task it was to protect inhabited areas, settlements, because they thought that in -- that clashes might ensue between neighbours and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. And then it says later on engage volunteers and -- "Approach and engage volunteers, carefully linking their engagement through the reserve police force when assessed as necessary, which means to exclude all voluntariness and arbitrary conduct." And the penultimate bullet point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask, what is meant by a volunteer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to answer, Your Honour? There are citizens who simply express the wish to become members of the army or police force, or join the army and police, especially in situations when problems are expected to arise such as aggression and so on and so forth, and we really did have people who came forward. They came to the police station and said they would like to join us and become members of the police force. Of course, both the army and the police has procedure in place and criteria for a reserve force. The mere fact that somebody wants to join up doesn't mean they'll be admitted to the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was this a particular feature of the time that this meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were always people like that, people interested in doing that, in joining the police force, even now. But of course a large number of them do not fulfil the criteria and are not taken on. We can even say that's the majority. The majority are not taken on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not understanding this at all. Either you get into the police or you don't get into -- surely in time of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you want to be a policeman, you become a policeman. So what's this particular reference here to approaching and engaging volunteers carefully, and why does it arise in the context of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was mentioned because of the fact that individuals like that can be suspect, so we must be careful of not admitting people who might act in a way that does not coincide with police ethics, and quite obviously people were interested in joining up, because this was mentioned. And I know for a fact myself that people came in to us, asking to be taken on board, even from abroad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, really I'm trying to find out was that something that happened around this time because of the NATO threat that was looming or are you saying that there was nothing unusual about that at this time, that this happened all the time? I mean, I find it a very strange comment in the context of this meeting unless it was a feature of the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I wasn't clear enough or perhaps I wasn't interpreted clearly enough. This is something that occurs at all times. Of course, just before a war, as indeed before events of this kind, the number of people interested in joining up was larger. There were more people wanting to join the police force to help the country in defending itself against an aggression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, before we break -- before we break, I have a quick question. About these bullet points of your forthcoming tasks, you referred to a passage which says, "We have to put our plans in motion and use the time to mop up the territory from terrorists." Is that very mopping up also "asanacija" in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course not. Asanacija is clearing up the terrain of human bodies and carcasses from livestock, and clearing up the territory of terrorists, the mop-up, means the anti-terrorist activities of the army and police to neutralise terrorist groups, apprehend the terrorists, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the B/C/S term for this mop-up, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Literally as it was interpreted. We say "cleaning up the territory of terrorism," of terrorist groups. It's a more complex concept, of course. It involves the uncovery, apprehension, taking into custody, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could I get the assistance from the interpreter as to the B/C/S for this mopping up? What word was used in the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not following the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The word "ciscenja --" I'm not following the interpretation. If you're asking about the word "ciscenja," then it is the most common use. In English, it would be "cleaning."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let me direct the interpreters to page 5. This is the page Judge Kwon was referring to, the end of the first paragraph, the penultimate sentence says: "Within two or three days of an attack we have to put our plans in motion and use the time to mop up the territory from terrorists." And Judge Kwon was asking the interpreters what was the B/C/S for the English words "mop up the territory from terrorists."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The word is "ocistimo," to clean up, to mop up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The word that is used is "ocistiti."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, that is precisely what I was quoting. I wasn't following the transcript but I quoted that sentence in B/C/S when I asked the general.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I can't find that portion of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I'll let you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we'll all be speaking B/C/S at the end of this case. But it is now time for the break. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, Mr. Robinson. Actually, they've drawn my attention to the fact that I should use the microphone on the left-hand side, but it seems to be making some kind of noise so I have to go back to the other one. I hope that you can hear me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand the microphone which is on now is the one that you will use.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Ah, this one. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's to your right. No? It's to his left?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, Mr. Robinson, you had some questions in relation to what had been quoted in tab 69. Have you finished? Would you like me to move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Thanks for the concern. Are you finished with 69?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I had finished before you put your questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Judge Bonomy has some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have one more question. One of the items on this document listing the tasks to be undertaken was "raise discipline, behaviour, and appearance of policemen to a high level. Do away with Rambo-style caps and bandannas." Was the wearing of that sort of clothing a problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there were cases of people wearing that kind of clothing. The entire staff, all the senior officers, were afraid of things like that happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's your answer, is it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did you attend the meeting held on the 4th of April at the staff? The minutes are in tab 70.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's evident that I attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can it be seen here that all the chiefs of secretariats were reporting at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: First the chief of Pristina secretariat?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then of Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just see a few of these things that he says. In the second Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. bullet after the beginning, in the third row, actually, "Measures were taken to curb terrorism and criminal acts."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "35 persons were detained." That means arrested; right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Three of whom are police officers and four members of the reserve composition." Towards the end of the page the chief of secretariat from Pec says: "11 persons were arrested because of crimes and 25 vehicles had been commandeered, probably those that were considered to be stolen.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the Djakovica secretariat says that 38 persons were arrested for perpetrating criminal acts?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in Prizren 19 persons?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the Urosevac secretariat says that 58 civilians and 8 volunteers were arrested?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In Gnjilane, 34 persons, and there was a problem with volunteers in Zegra.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the perpetrators of the crime that we referred to, but perhaps the word "volunteers" is used wrongly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In what sense?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they were members of the military. Perhaps they volunteered to join the army but they did not act as members of the military outside the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And then it says about 50.000 persons moved out and about 15.000 persons were returned from the Vranje area. And then paragraph 2 says "Tasks in the future." Is it General Lukic, the head of the staff, speaking at the end?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does he say at the very outset? "In wartime the Ministry of the Interior carries out all its work as in peacetime." I hope you've found that. "Has the same attitude to perpetrators of criminal acts as in peacetime, regardless of their ethnicity. Courts will receive instructions on further work in the course of the day."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then the fourth bullet from the bottom of the page: "Rigorous measures to be taken against paramilitary units."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this a general statement, a general position?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A general position that was always made clear because of bad experience from the previous wars with such groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There's a reference to you on the last page. It says "Obrad Stevanovic, assistant minister."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And now, along with the other tasks that you talk about, you say in the sixth bullet: "Protection of civilians is to be carried out at all times."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, may I take you back to the bullet indicating measures to be taken against paramilitary units, and you said that was necessary in the light of previous experience. Can you tell me, enlighten me as to some of that experience with paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was assumed that paramilitary units outside the Republic of Serbia that are not under the control of appropriate military or civilian organs could be the perpetrators of gravest crimes. That was the assumption. We did not have any concrete data, but that was the prevailing conviction. The idea was to place them all either under the control of the military or of the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So it wasn't based on any actual experience, because I thought you said that these measures were necessary because of experience that you had had with paramilitary units in previous -- previous wars.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not because of our own experience, but I can actually mention some experience --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, can I quote you as saying, you said, "That was always made clear because of bad experience from the previous wars with such groups." You said so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. I can explain. I can be very specific about this. We had a general impression of these groups in very general terms, but I'm going to give some specific incidents as well. Paramilitary groups from Republika Srpska, during 1992 and 1993, carried out the well-known attacks against the bus in Mloce near Rudo and they abducted about 17 or 18 civilians. Later these persons went missing and have been missing to the present day. Paramilitary groups also attacked a Yugoslav train on the Belgrade-Bar railway way in the village of Strpce, which happens to be in the territory of Republika Srpska and similarly kidnapped civilians. As far as I know, they have been missing until the present day. I can give a few other incidents of this kind but I would need some time to recall them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What were the characteristics of paramilitary unit? Yes. I was asking how would you define a paramilitary unit, or could you tell us the characteristics, the features of such a unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was also one of the problems involved. The question is what is denoted by this. I can say at the very outset that we considered irregular groups to be that. They had military insignia but they were not under the official command of the military or of the police in the state concerned. Of course, we were aware of the fact that this word can denote some regular forms, like the police. In foreign literature and in foreign countries, even the police can be meant by that term. Our interpretation was groups that wore uniforms, that carried weapons but were outside the military chain of command or perhaps were not even under police command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You said that they had military insignia. How have they come by military insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It must have been a misinterpretation. I said military uniforms and carried weapons but possibly they also had some insignia, some insignia. I cannot recall any of the insignia at this moment because I did not see a person myself whom I would say belonged to a paramilitary unit in terms of uniform, weapons, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If they did have military insignia, how would they have come by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It depends on what kind of military insignia we mean. They had insignia, but I didn't say of any particular army. Every paramilitary group calls itself a certain name and then they make their own insignia. I repeat, I never had occasion to see anyone like that. If they had insignia of the army, then they would belong to the army, they would not be paramilitary. That is most probably what the case would be. I don't think that an army would allow a paramilitary group to wear its insignia, although abuse of this kind is always possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, the two specific examples you gave relating to the Republika Srpska, were these examples of Serb paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, we've dealt with this now, and then General Lukic says: "During the war, the MUP does all its work as in peacetime, has the same attitude towards perpetrators or criminal acts in peacetime regardless of their ethnicity." What you say also, civilians should be protected at all times.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a bit difficult for me to follow these minutes, I am sorry, because I saw them just now. Obviously they were submitted through the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because they have the appropriate number on the top.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had occasion to see them or read them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But I'm sure that you recognise this to be a meeting that you attended?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I imagine that this is not being challenged?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you attend the meeting at the staff on the 7th of May in Pristina? The minutes in tab 71. It also has an ERN number.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did attend the meeting. That can be seen on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We can see from here that this meeting was attended, among others, by the deputy federal Prime Minister, it says in the first line, Mr. Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There are many quotations here from his contribution to that meeting. I will draw your attention only to a few of them. Namely, at the beginning it reads: "Mr. Nikola Sainovic said..." In the sixth paragraph below, it says: "Apart from destroying the terrorist organisation KLA, our main task will be to secure peace in Kosovo and Metohija. This must be felt by both our citizens and the entire world."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic. Mr. Milosevic, I've already told you you are not to proceed until the Chamber has found the passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: English page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Page 4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just over halfway down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You may continue. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Further below, towards the end of that paragraph, it says: "Securing stable public law and order and securing citizens and their property must be done by the MUP because we cannot allow the Serbs to be stigmatised --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise, we haven't found this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's on page 5 at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You attended that meeting. It says: "Health care must be ensured. Food and medicine must be delivered to those who have abandoned their homes because of the bombing and terrorist actions."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I will not quote more, but he says that during the first days of the bombing, the terrorists, led by Hashim Thaci, signalled the terrorists to launch a general attack on civilian facilities, et cetera. A great number of casualties in consequences. Next quotation: "Organise the life of the Albanian population in villages and settlements where the population lives in by registering their places of residence. The loyalty of Albanians towards the state rests on organised life. The goal of organising the Albanian population is that when refugees return, they can come back to a regulated situation in which people have already registered their place of residence. Demand that Albanians establish a body or local commune in each village and that they set up a local authority and local police in grey uniforms to maintain law and order. Record the number of settlements that have been organised in this way and the number of those that haven't had the time."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We talked about that when we discussed the campaign to have citizens register in their new places of residence, the temporary places of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Three paragraphs below, it says: "Organise mix and organise patrols to check all uniformed and motorised persons. Every uniformed persons must be held accountable for theft because with his uniform he brings shame not only upon himself but upon the state. Those in charge of the police bear great objective responsibility and this responsibility is appreciated if it is said that a specific task cannot be done and why, instead of remaining unsaid." Do we see here another instance of the authorities urging lawful action and proper application of the regulations?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an example of how the authorities insist that the police and the military act always in conformity with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't have time to quote much more, but I will end with the conclusions of the leader of the staff, General -- Major General Lukic, who stressed the following: "Speaking of cases and incidents with serious consequences --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the beginning of the section dealing with the contribution of Major General Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note page 22.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian version, it's the third page from the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Regarding cases involving grave consequences, everything must be processed as seriously as possible."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot find this particular passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The interpreters can't find it. We're looking at -- we're looking at a paragraph beginning, "In his closing speech, the head of staff, Major Lukic, said..." Is that where you're reading from?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note page 19, towards the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Page 19.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am reading what it says here: "When cases and incidents result in grave consequences, they must be processed in a very -- in a way suitable to these working conditions." Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we've found it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Regardless of whether the act was carried out by terrorists, whether persons died in the army of Yugoslavia and MUP clashes with terrorists or whether these are consequences of NATO bombing, or even crimes of murder under the Criminal Code," et cetera. He also says: "The number of 27 crimes of murder is not realistic as we have information that a greater number of on-site investigations has been conducted and that the number of criminal reports concerning this crime is greater." Is this another indication that actions were lawful?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the number 27 sounds too small, and he urges the police to record every incident and take appropriate action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General Lukic goes on to say that in cases involving arson and murder there should be no delay. The suspects must be handed over to the competent judge at once and, "You must ask for a sentence to be pronounced immediately.
