These sorts of problems have still not be cleared up, especially in Kosovo Polje and Podujevo and Prizren and Djakovica, while Gnjilane has clearly resolved some problems." Next bullet: "Based on the above, it has clearly been stated and specified that no omissions in any case will be tolerated or forgiven." It is an expression in our language that means nobody should be given any leeway or margin of error.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I read this at the time, although it was a long time ago and I couldn't remember the details until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Follows your contribution. You say: "Crime prevention, especially of crimes involving violence and anarchy, is a police priority, because the internal affairs organs shall be held responsible for every broken shop window and each murder." You go on to speak of anti-terrorist actions, about the sanitisation of battlefields, building of defences, preparation of defence against aggression by ground forces. And towards the end of your contribution you suggest that supervisory units be organised in order to be able to take specific measures in case of misconduct by the police. That means an internal control body within the police.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This meeting was held on the 7th of May, when the working conditions were the hardest, and still the leadership insists on lawfulness in the conduct of the police.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is clear from the passages of these minutes that you quoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did you attend the meeting at the ministry staff of the 11th of May? It's tab 72.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was the agenda of that meeting? Let me just draw your attention to a couple of things. The tasks include -- or, rather, the tasks are related to the defence of the country, anti-terrorist struggle Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and the establishment of general security in Kosovo and Metohija. Measures undertaken to prevent crime and maintain public law and order in a state of war. Reports are made at this meeting by?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the special police units detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Here the pages are not numbered, but I can use the ERN number. In fact, they are numbered but this is a bad copy. The ERN number is K0497277. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My copy is bad as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In Mr. Nice's service, something was probably glued on top of this, so one part is hidden. This is your contribution. Under item 2, you say: "The incidence of crime was especially discussed at the meeting with chiefs of secretariats. It was said that a case file has to be compiled for every incident. Private wars should be banned because the reputation of the police must be protected and civilians must not be afraid of the police. Special action should be taken to prevent arsons and looting." And you stress how important it is to observe the law in every respect in performing policework. You go on to say that all citizens must be treated lawfully, whereas able-bodied men will be the subject of special checks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the page?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the last page but one in the Serbian version, which has a total of seven pages, and it is from the contribution of General Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Page 14.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I said where I'm reading from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 3: "Departure of civilians ought to be prevented as much as possible." The rest of the text illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you go on to say: "All citizens are to be treated pursuant to the law." I have already quoted this.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Follows some organisational and personnel issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just point out one thing, because Mr. Bonomy expressed a special interest in paramilitary units. General Lukic stresses in the last paragraph of these minutes: "Prohibit the wearing of uniforms by any person who is not an authorised police member or a member of the reserve police force who has been mobilised." How was it possible, General, that there still existed people who wore uniforms and did not have the status of policemen?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume that such groups could exist because the conditions in Kosovo and Metohija during the war were very complex and very difficult, and it was difficult to exercise control over the entire territory in every smallest place, and I don't say that they existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That was tab 72, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How about the conclusions of that meeting of the 17th and the 11th -- of the 7th and the 11th of May? Were they delivered to the personnel on the ground?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well that the conclusions were made available to all the personnel on the ground to be followed and acted upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 73 can we find the minutes of the meeting or, rather, the conclusions of the meeting? It says: "At meetings held on 7th and 11th of May, 1999."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is a list of conclusions from both meetings we've just analysed, meetings of the 7th and 11th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's the 11th of May. In item 1, it says: "The whole leadership must be informed of the text of the communications from the meeting held with the President of the FRY." We have already reviewed that text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have been over this already. Move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I have received from the office of Mr. Nice a copy of your own agenda where you kept your notes, your organiser. I would like to ask you a couple of questions about those notes, and they are these: To what extent if at all can we see in those notebooks the care for the civilians, equal treatment for all citizens, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the original text of my agenda or notebook this can be seen very easily. It's clearly visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that's your own personal diary or agenda where you make your own notes in your own handwriting as an aide-memoire. So can we see there, then, that efforts were made to prevent crime generally?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly that can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And can we also see that you are investing efforts to bring the perpetrators of crime to justice?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although I don't have the opportunity of following the case through, or following these cases through, because I didn't have my agenda. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I think that Mr. Nice would have to explain why he's seeking a private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can we go into private session. The matter is the subject of a motion that's been before the Chamber. It's been before the accused. It's been before the amici, and it's extremely disturbing, matters are being dealt with in this way, but nevertheless. I'm going to ask that everything that's been said about the diary from about the last couple of questions is redacted as well, but can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is the subject of a motion by the Prosecutor, and we had indicated that when the matter arose we would deal with it, but we're going to deal with it in private session. The Prosecutor will then explain his position. Go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would really like to ask you something. May I be allowed to say just one sentence, and I have my own security and safety reasons for saying this, for saying what I want to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are in public session. We are in public session. Should we return to private session to hear you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't mind. I don't mind being in open session to say what I have to say. And it is in my interests that everything we state here should be in open session, and I accept not to mention a single name because that is not an important point for me. But I would like to ask your permission for me to be able to say one sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. I think we need to be in private session for that. Let's go back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00 a.m. Oh, I see. Apparently it's 2.15 tomorrow. 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 27th day of May, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.43 p.m.,
